matched_queries: UK employment guidance: Regulating umbrella companies and explaining responsibilities when employing or paying workers through an umbrella company.

passages.quote:
This guidance explains how to complete the questions in the Company Share Option Plan (CSOP) Employment Related Securities (ERS) annual end of year return. It also identifies which questions are mandatory, conditional mandatory or optional.

There have been some changes made to the end of year return headings. If you wish to create your own end of year template, check the (From April 2027) Company Share Option Plan: Technical notes — from the 2023 to 2024 tax year for more information.

The current CSOP end of year return from the 2023 to 2024 tax year is version 7.

1. Who must submit the end of year return

The company secretary, or the person acting as company secretary, must submit an online CSOP ERS end of year return by 6 July following the end of the tax year.

In circumstances where the employee is employed by an Employer of Record (EoR), the EoR is responsible for submitting the returns.

An end of year return must be submitted for each registered and self-certified CSOP scheme.

2. When to submit an end of year return or a nil return

If you operate an ERS scheme, you are required to submit an end of year ERS return, including nil returns, for every scheme registered.

If your scheme has ended and you have entered a final event date, you must submit any outstanding returns up until the date that it ended.

3. Completing and uploading your end of year return

You can use the Employment related securities (ERS) checking service to check your end of year return.

The service:

shows where formatting errors occur which will prevent your end of year return being submitted successfully

can be used as often as needed

helps you correct errors early, making submission easier

You can also access the checking service through ‘View my schemes and arrangements’ on the online ERS service.

4. General guidance on valuations

All values must be entered in pounds sterling to 4 decimal places.

Where necessary:

round up figures ending in 5 or more

round down figures ending in 4 or less

If a value is quoted in another currency, use a reputable currency converter to convert it to pounds sterling.

You do not need to formally agree valuations of shares and securities with HMRC.

Where shares are not listed on a recognised stock exchange, you may have asked HMRC for a valuation. If a valuation was agreed with HMRC:

enter the valuation reference number on the end of year return

if the reference is prefixed with Company Reference Number (CRN), do not enter those letters

If no valuation was agreed, you must retain records showing how the valuation was reasonably determined.

4.1 Actual Market Value (AMV)

AMV is the value of a share or security after taking account of:

restrictions

risk of forfeiture

4.2 Unrestricted Market Value (UMV)

UMV is the value of a share or security ignoring:

restrictions

risk of forfeiture

4.3 Recognised stock exchanges

For more information about recognised stock exchanges read Recognised stock exchanges: definition, legislation and tables.

AIM (Alternative Investment Market) and PISCES (Private Intermittent Securities and Capital Exchange System) are not recognised stock exchanges for these purposes.

5. General guidance on completing the end of year return

5.1 Mandatory, conditional mandatory, and optional fields

Mandatory — a response is always required regardless of any other information provided.

Conditional Mandatory — a response is only required if you have provided a response to a mandatory question. For example, if a share option has been granted in a CSOP then the ‘Date of Grant’ would need to be reported.

Optional — this field can be left blank but should be completed if you know the information requested.

If a conditional mandatory or optional field does not require a response, leave it blank.

Do not enter:

‘N/A’

‘not applicable’

Doing so will cause your end of year return to be rejected.

5.2 Yes and no answers

The following formats are accepted:

Yes, yes, YES

No, no, NO

6. Common worksheet fields

6.1 Employee first name

This is the employee’s first name.

This field is mandatory.

6.2 Employee second name (optional).

If the employee has a second name, then enter in this column.

This field is optional.

6.3 Employee last name

This is the employee’s last name.

This field is mandatory.

6.4 National Insurance number

Enter in the correct format — for example, QQ123456C

Most individuals included on an ERS end of year return will have a National Insurance number. In exceptional cases, use an alternative reference instead.

This reference must:

only be used on the ERS end of year return

not be used in any other HMRC correspondence

not be given to the individual

Where there are exceptional circumstances, the required format for the alternative ERS reference will be a total of 9 characters. This will be 2 letters, 6 numbers and one letter consisting of:

TN – to indicate an ERS reference

employee date of birth in format DDMMYY (for example, 080403) ― this data will enable HMRC to trace the individual

no National Insurance number reason identifier (X, Y or Z) ― this is to identify the reason why an individual does not have a National Insurance number

X ― under 16 years old

Y ― applied for a National Insurance number and is waiting to receive it

Z — never paid National Insurance contributions as they have not been liable to UK National Insurance contributions ― for example, they’re not resident in the UK or are an ‘intra-company worker’ on transfer to work in the UK

This field is mandatory.

7. Worksheet specific guidance

The following sections explain when to use each worksheet and how to complete its questions.

Use a separate row for each individual unless stated otherwise.

(All worksheet definitions, questions, routing rules, thresholds, examples and calculations remain unchanged and are presented in a clearer sequence below.)

This field is mandatory.

10. CSOP_OptionsExercised_V7 worksheet

Use this to tell HMRC about options exercised in the tax year.

10.1 Question 1: Date of event

Enter the date option was exercised by the employee.

Use the format yyyy‑mm‑dd — for example, 2023-10-31.

This field is mandatory.

10.2 Question 2 to 5

Check the common fields guidance under section 6.

10.6 Question 6: PAYE reference of employing company

Enter the PAYE reference number of the company that employs the employee.

The employing company should be the company that has the PAYE obligation.

This field is mandatory.

10.7 Question 7: Date of grant.

Enter the format yyyy‑mm‑dd — for example, 2023‑10‑31.

Enter the date the CSOP options were granted to the employees.

The date of grant will be shown on the option certificate.

Options granted on the same date can be reported in one row, provided the Unrestricted Market Value (UMV) of the security is the same for all options granted on that date.

This field is mandatory.

10.8 Question 8: Total number of shares employee entitled to on exercise of the option before any cashless exercise or other adjustment

Enter the number to 2 decimal places — for example, 100.00.

This is the gross number of shares and includes shares sold as part of a cashless exercise procedure to pay for Income Tax and National Insurance contributions or the exercise price.

For example, an employee has options over 200 shares and choses to exercise the option to acquire 100 shares. 40 of those shares are immediately sold as part of a cashless exercise procedure to pay for the employee’s Income Tax and National Insurance contributions liability. You would enter 100 in this field.

This field is optional.

10.9 Question 9: Are these shares part of the largest class of shares in that company?

Enter yes or no.

Some companies create different classes of ordinary share, for example ’A’ and ‘B’ ordinary shares.

The largest class of share is the class of shares with entitlement to the largest proportion of value (£) on a winding-up.

If you only have one class of share, enter ‘yes’. If you have more than one class of shares and they are equal in value enter ‘yes’.

This field is mandatory.

10.10 Question 10: Are the shares subject to the option listed on recognised stock exchange?

Enter yes or no.

For more information read Recognised stock exchanges: definition, legislation and tables. AIM and PISCES are not recognised stock exchanges for these purposes.

This field is mandatory.

10.11 Question 11: AMV of a share on the date of exercise

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places — for example, 10.1234.

This field is optional.

10.12 Question 12: Exercise price per share

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places — for example, 10.1234.

Enter the price at which the employee was granted the option. It is the price the employee will pay for each share on the exercise of the share option.

If the exercise price is set in a currency that is not GBP (£), use a reputable currency converter to obtain the GBP (£) value as of the date of exercise.

This field is optional.

10.13 Question 13: UMV of a share on the date of exercise

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places — for example, 10.1234.

This field is optional.

10.14 Question 14: If the answer to question 10 is ‘no’, was the market value agreed with HMRC?

Enter yes or no.

If you enter ‘yes’ go to question 15. If you enter ‘no’ go to question 16.

This field is conditional mandatory.

10.15 Question 15: If yes, enter the HMRC valuation reference given

The HMRC valuation reference is shown on the valuation letter issued by the Shares and Assets Valuation office.

The reference will usually be your Company Reference Number (CRN).

Enter the reference exactly as shown, including any letters and numbers. If the reference begins with 3 letters, enter numbers only.

This field is conditional mandatory.

10.16 Question 16: Does the exercise qualify for tax relief?

Enter yes or no.

The answer will be yes if the option is exercised:

between the third and tenth anniversary of the date of grant

by a good leaver, subject to the scheme rules, before the third anniversary of the date of grant

This field is mandatory.

10.17 Question 17: Was PAYE operated?

Enter yes or no.

PAYE should have been operated if the shares are readily convertible into cash and the full relief is not available.

If you enter ‘no’, go to question 20.

This field is mandatory.

10.18 Question 18: If yes, deductible amount

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places — for example, 10.1234

You must enter the total amount of any:

amount paid for the grant of the option

expenses incurred for the acquisition of the securities

You must not enter any:

exercise price also often referred to as grant or strike price

expenses in connection with the sale or disposal of the securities

Employers National Insurance contributions the employee may have agreed to pay under a joint National Insurance contribution agreement or election

Income Tax

This field is conditional mandatory.

10.19 Question 19: Has a National Insurance contributions election or agreement been operated?

Enter yes or no.

This is when the employer and the employee agree or jointly elect for the employee to meet the employer’s liability to pay secondary National Insurance contributions on certain types of share awards and share options gains. The employee can then get a deduction equal to the amount of secondary or employers’ National Insurance contributions transferred when working out the amount chargeable to Income Tax.

This field is mandatory.

10.20 Question 20: Were all shares resulting from the exercise sold?

Enter yes or no.
